title: Claude Code extension surfaces
subtitle: How context, scope, tools, and controls shape a working session
footer: Sources: current Claude Code docs • context, memory, settings, skills, subagents, hooks, MCP • 2026-08-22

bands.heading: Claude Code is an agent loop wrapped in an extension layer
bands.deck: Artifacts change what the model sees, what tools exist, and what must happen

callouts.label: What enters context
callouts.note: instructions, files, summaries, and returned tool output

callouts.label: What stays external
callouts.note: hooks run as code unless they return context

image.use: Show a developer operating inside a repository-shaped environment surrounded by context, tools, controls, and state.
image.description: Paper-cut developer control room showing context, tools, trust, state, and extension sources around one working session.

visual.explanation: Claude Code starts with built-in tools for reading, editing, searching, executing. The extension layer changes the loop at different points: some artifacts enter the prompt, some add tools, some isolate work, some run around tool calls.
visual.example: Invoking a review skill adds its instructions to context; a subagent keeps the file reads separate and returns only a summary.
visual.tradeoff: Every extension adds context, tools, trust, or maintenance cost; bigger is not automatically better.
visual.caption: Choose an artifact by where it enters the loop, not by its filename.

bands.heading: The context window is the budget every artifact competes for
bands.deck: Loading time matters because context affects cost, attention, and compaction

visual.explanation: Claude's context holds the system prompt, persistent instructions, conversation, file contents, and tool results. They do not cost the same: descriptions and tool names are light; full files and invoked skill bodies are large.
visual.example: A research subagent reads dozens of files in its own window and returns a short summary instead of flooding the main conversation.
visual.tradeoff: After compaction only root instructions re-inject; always-on context costs every request, on-demand mechanisms need the right trigger.
visual.caption: Context is a managed working set, not an unlimited knowledge base.

bands.heading: Scope answers two questions: who receives it, and where it applies
bands.deck: Managed, user, project, and local artifacts differ in ownership and blast radius

visual.explanation: Scope is not one universal hierarchy. Settings use managed, CLI, local, project, user precedence; instructions are additive; skills and subagents override by name; MCP has its own order.
visual.example: A personal formatting preference lives in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; a team build command in the repository's CLAUDE.md; a sandbox URL in CLAUDE.local.md.
visual.tradeoff: Broad scope increases reuse and blast radius. Narrow scope improves relevance but is easier to overlook.
visual.caption: Choose scope from ownership and sharing needs before choosing a filename.
visual.thesis: Every artifact lands somewhere on one plane: how late it loads sets what it costs the main window.

bands.heading: The `.claude` hierarchy maps scope; it is not one precedence ladder
bands.deck: User, project, and nested paths decide ownership, sharing, and when context becomes visible

visual.focus: A filesystem map with several loading rules

nodes.label: ~/.claude/
nodes.note: personal context and defaults across projects

nodes.label: repo/.claude/
nodes.note: rules, skills, agents, workflows, and settings

nodes.label: packages/billing/
nodes.note: nested context activated by file access

callouts.label: User-owned
callouts.note: CLAUDE.md, settings, skills, agents, and rules under ~/.claude/

callouts.label: Project-owned
callouts.note: CLAUDE.md, .claude/, and root .mcp.json can be reviewed in git

callouts.label: Private project state
callouts.note: CLAUDE.local.md and settings.local.json stay out of version control

visual.explanation: The filesystem tells you ownership and discovery, not one precedence ladder. User artifacts live under ~/.claude; project instructions at repo/CLAUDE.md or repo/.claude/; shared rules and settings under repo/.claude; MCP servers in .mcp.json. Nested directories activate near matching files.
visual.example: A billing task combines ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, repo/CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, and packages/billing/CLAUDE.md without any replacing the others.
visual.tradeoff: One override ladder fails for additive instructions, merged hooks, named skills, and MCP servers.
visual.caption: Map the files first; apply each artifact's own loading rule second.
visual.thesis: The four scopes sit on two axes, control versus specificity, not one ladder.

bands.heading: CLAUDE.md and auto memory are complementary context, not enforcement
bands.deck: One is authored policy; the other is Claude's repository-specific learning

visual.thesis: One repository, four ownership zones; each zone loads by its own rule.
visual.focus: Persistent context, not a hard control
visual.explanation: CLAUDE.md carries facts every session needs: build commands, conventions, stable guidance. Auto memory records corrections Claude cannot derive from the repository. Both are prompt context, still interpreted, never enforced.
visual.example: Put 'run pnpm test before committing' in project CLAUDE.md; block an unsafe command with a PreToolUse hook rather than prose.
visual.tradeoff: Long always-on instructions reduce adherence; procedures belong in skills. Memory loads capped at 200 lines.
visual.caption: Write what every session must know; enforce what every session must obey.

bands.heading: CLAUDE.md loading is additive and path-sensitive
bands.deck: Launch location establishes the baseline; subtree reads activate local context

nodes.label: Local file
nodes.note: appended after CLAUDE.md at that level

nodes.label: Nested files
nodes.note: load only when subtree files are read

callouts.label: Focused district
callouts.note: billing context activates near billing files

image.use: Show a monorepo as a city whose shared root remains visible while the billing package gains local detail.
image.description: Top-down repository city whose illuminated billing district shows how path-scoped instructions narrow to one package.

visual.explanation: Claude loads ancestor instructions at launch; nested instructions join when matching files are read.
visual.example: Start in billing to load root and billing files; start at repo, then read invoice.ts to activate billing.
visual.tradeoff: Nested context focuses a monorepo but must be re-triggered after compaction.
visual.caption: Directory position controls when instruction context becomes active.

bands.heading: CLAUDE.md, rules, and skills differ mainly by loading behavior
bands.deck: Use the cheapest context mechanism that still triggers reliably

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md
items: Full content loads at session start
Best for core commands, architecture, and conventions
Keep roughly under 200 lines; imports still consume startup context
Example: package manager and mandatory test command

nodes.label: .claude/rules/
items: Unscoped rules load every session; paths rules load with matching files
Best for language, directory, and security-specific guidance
Recursive discovery supports frontend/ and backend/ organization
Inspect paths frontmatter and trigger by reading a matching file

nodes.label: Skill
items: Description loads at start; full SKILL.md loads when used
Best for reusable knowledge and repeatable workflows
May be invoked as /name or loaded automatically when relevant
Example: deployment checklist or API reference
Inspect the skill source and invoke it explicitly to test

bands.heading: Settings precedence resolves values; it is not a workflow
bands.deck: Scalar winners, merged arrays, and restrictive exceptions need separate explanations

visual.focus: Layered settings resolve one effective configuration

nodes.label: Security exception
nodes.note: restrictive value may win outside normal order

nodes.label: Managed tier
nodes.note: organization delivery has its own source rules

callouts.label: Not one rule
callouts.note: merge behavior depends on the setting's type

image.use: Show settings as translucent authoritative layers, with merged-array strands and a restrictive safety clamp as separate exception motifs.
image.description: Translucent configuration layers resolving into one value beside separate merge strands and a restrictive safety clamp.

visual.explanation: Scalar settings choose a higher-precedence value; arrays merge; safety keys can honor restrictive lower values.
visual.example: A project disables spinner tips, overriding user settings; permissions.allow entries combine.
visual.tradeoff: One precedence list misleads for arrays and security exceptions.
visual.caption: Model settings as layered resolution rules, not boxes causing one another.

bands.heading: Skills are on-demand capabilities with their own discovery and precedence
bands.deck: A skill's location controls ownership; its description controls when Claude loads it

visual.focus: One command name can exist at several levels
visual.explanation: Skills package knowledge or workflows in SKILL.md; descriptions load at startup, full bodies only when invoked. Name conflicts resolve by source: enterprise over personal, personal over project, skill over command; plugin skills are namespaced.
visual.example: A root /deploy skill coexists with apps/web/.claude/skills/deploy, which appears as apps/web:deploy near that package.
visual.tradeoff: Broad personal skills can unexpectedly override project behavior; project skills are reviewable but repo-bound.
visual.caption: Skills are a loading and ownership system, not just saved prompts.
visual.thesis: Skill discovery is a neighborhood: location sets ownership, description sets loading.

bands.heading: Subagents buy context isolation, not merely parallel speed
bands.deck: A specialized worker has its own prompt, tools, permissions, and context window

visual.thesis: The main window stays small because subagents absorb the reads and return summaries.

callouts.label: Isolation
callouts.note: large file reads stay outside the main conversation

callouts.label: Return value
callouts.note: only the summary and metadata come back

callouts.label: Specialization
callouts.note: preload relevant skills and restrict tools

visual.explanation: A subagent runs its own loop with separate context, system prompt, tools, and permissions — useful when a side task would flood the main conversation or needs a specialized worker repeatedly. The parent receives a summary, not the trace.
visual.example: Send a codebase-wide search to a read-only research subagent; the main conversation receives only relevant symbols, risks, and paths.
visual.tradeoff: Isolation hides intermediate reasoning. Parent permission mode and managed policy still constrain the subagent.
visual.caption: Delegate when the intermediate work is expensive but the result is small.

bands.heading: Hooks and permissions are the enforcement plane
bands.deck: Prompt instructions guide judgment; runtime controls can block an operation

visual.focus: Guidance and enforcement occupy different sides of the boundary

callouts.label: Guidance
callouts.note: CLAUDE.md and skills can influence judgment

callouts.label: Enforcement
callouts.note: permissions and hooks can deny unsafe action

image.use: Contrast a soft cloud of guidance with a physical enforcement checkpoint and a human decision between them.
image.description: Handcrafted scene contrasting soft guidance with a lockable enforcement gate and a deliberate human decision.

visual.explanation: Hooks are event-driven automation: a lifecycle event, a matcher, one or more handlers. PreToolUse runs after tool parameters exist but before the call processes, so it can allow, deny, ask, or defer. Permissions are the other deterministic layer.
visual.example: A PreToolUse hook rejects destructive shell commands and returns the reason; a PostToolUse hook lints an edit and feeds the result back.
visual.tradeoff: @ file references do not fire Read hooks; block the path itself with a Read deny rule instead.
visual.caption: Use prose for judgment and runtime controls for guarantees.

bands.heading: MCP, skills, and plugins extend different layers
bands.deck: Connections, operating knowledge, and distribution should not be conflated

visual.thesis: Claude Code is a hub; MCP, skills, and plugins are satellites extending different layers of one product.
visual.explanation: MCP connects external services and actions. A skill teaches how and when to use them. A plugin packages skills, hooks, subagents, and servers for distribution. Duplicate server names resolve local before project before user; no field merging.
visual.example: Commit a project-scoped server to .mcp.json so the team shares the connection; add a skill documenting safe query patterns.
visual.tradeoff: External tools enlarge the trust surface; environment expansion adds flexibility, secrets and approvals need review.
visual.inspect: Run claude mcp list and claude mcp get <name>; inspect .mcp.json.
visual.caption: Connect the system, teach the workflow, package the setup.

bands.heading: Worked example: editing packages/billing/invoice.ts
bands.deck: Different artifacts enter at startup, on file access, on invocation, and on events

visual.thesis: One edit pulls four artifact kinds into context at four different moments.

nodes.label: Startup
nodes.note: root memory, auto memory, descriptions, tool names

nodes.label: Invocation
nodes.note: selected skill body + MCP schema on use

nodes.label: Isolation
nodes.note: subagent summary returns without its full reads

visual.explanation: Before the prompt Claude holds root instructions, auto memory, skill descriptions, and tool names. Reading invoice.ts activates billing CLAUDE.md and path rules; invoking a skill adds its body; an MCP call loads its schema; hooks run at events.
visual.example: A billing review reads invoice.ts, activates packages/billing/CLAUDE.md, invokes /review-invoice, queries an accounting MCP tool, runs a post-edit hook.
visual.tradeoff: Each layer aids specialization but adds a debug surface; existing on disk does not prove a file loaded or won precedence.
visual.caption: Debug the effective session, not the directory tree in isolation.

bands.heading: Choose the artifact by load behavior, context cost, and trust
bands.deck: The narrowest mechanism that reliably triggers is usually the best one

visual.explanation: Start from the trigger. Every session needs a fact: CLAUDE.md. Only matching files: a path rule. Occasional procedure: a skill. Expensive side work: a subagent. Must always happen or block: a hook or permission rule.
visual.example: Keep a 100-line deployment playbook as /deploy, branch protection in a hook or CI, and delegate environment research to a subagent.
visual.tradeoff: The narrowest mechanism reduces noise, but too much fragmentation makes the setup hard to discover. Keep ownership and inspection commands visible.
visual.inspect: Run /context; inspect CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, and the selected hook.
visual.caption: Design the effective agent loop, not a decorative .claude folder.
